answer: Rate-limit identity creation: new identities join a queue that admits only a set number per epoch, and each must mature through epochs of verified service before earning full standing. A sybil operator faces a hollow queue: thousands of clones stuck waiting, unable to act. Like a mesa, the admission rate is flat and cannot be climbed by spending more; the queue does not bend to wealth. Meanwhile waiting turns a one-time forgery into a spiral of upkeep: every clone needs continuous work across epochs to stay eligible, so the cost of a fake army grows with time while its power stays capped.
